_doc: Expected RESOLVED dispatch per ISA class, keyed by the isa_class that
`mynah-tts --dispatch-map --json` prints. tools/dispatch_gate.py compares this
against an observed report and fails when a feature that is expected ON, is
compiled AND supported on the host, resolves OFF anyway.
That shape -- have the unit, have the kernel, run neither -- is the one this
project keeps producing and cannot see: on 2026-09-22 an EPYC 9254 ran a bf16
kernel it reported as unimplemented, and called a unit two kernels require
'idle hardware'. Neither broke a test, because no test knew what the table
was supposed to say.
A class absent here is checked by the generic rules only. Values are ON, OFF,
or a prefix of the resolved string for value rows (e.g. 'avx512' matches
'avx512vnni').
Rows that are ALTERNATIVES for one job. At most one may be ON, and a
member reading OFF beside a winner is the correct answer, not a gap --
so the SUSPICIOUS rule fires for a group only when EVERY member is OFF
while at least one is compiled and supported here.
Written because the gate failed a docs-only commit on 2026-09-22: the
GitHub x86 runner pool is heterogeneous, that run landed on a machine
with AVX-VNNI *and* AVX-512 VNNI, and the gate called isa.x86.avxvnni
suspicious for losing to the wider kernel. A gate that cries wolf gets
switched off, which would have cost more than the bug it was built for.
